label: Scoped certificate calibration connects a procedure to exact classification
paraphrase: For arbitrary state and evidence types, procedure coverage and accepted-certificate calibration on an explicit scope imply exact classification on that scope subtype; the availability field inside coverage is not used for this conclusion. Finite controls exhibit a nonvacuous covered calibrated procedure, coverage without calibration, an extensionally classifiable norm (the identity criterion for s = true) together with an always-true echo procedure that lacks resources and so is not covered (it would also fail calibration for that norm), showing that extensional classifiability does not imply coverage by a given procedure, and calibration on a restricted scope without calibration on all states. Certificate acceptance is not philosophical warrant.
